subject: general
question: On 24 January 2025, which day was celebrated to promote girls’ rights and welfare in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**National Girl Child Day**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **National Girl Child Day **is celebrated in India every year on **24th January** to promote awareness about the rights, education, and health of girl children.
 
• It was first initiated by the **Ministry of Women and Child Development** in 2008 to highlight the issues faced by girls in India and to empower them.
 
• The day emphasizes addressing **gender-based discrimination** and promoting gender equality in all aspects of society.
 
• Various campaigns and events are organized across the country to spread awareness about the importance of saving, educating, and empowering the girl child.
 
• The celebration aligns with the goals of government schemes like **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao**, which focuses on improving the welfare and status of girls in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Beti Bachao Beti Padhao (BBBP):**

 
 
• Launched in 2015, it aims to address declining **Child Sex Ratio (CSR)** and promote the survival, protection, and education of the girl child.
 
• The campaign is a tri-ministerial effort involving the Ministries of Women and Child Development, Health and Family Welfare, and Education.
 
 
 
• **Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (SSY):**
 
 
• A government-backed savings scheme aimed at securing the future of girl children.
 
• Parents can open an account for a girl child below 10 years, with benefits like tax exemptions and high-interest rates.
 
 
 
• **Gender Inequality in India:**
 
 
• India has faced challenges like **female infanticide, child marriage, and gender-based violence**, which these initiatives aim to address.
 
• Promoting girl child education and empowerment is pivotal to achieving societal progress and economic development.
 
 
 
• **United Nations International Day of the Girl Child:**
 
 
• Celebrated globally on **11th October**, it complements India's National Girl Child Day by advocating for girls' rights worldwide.
 
• The focus is on issues like education, healthcare access, and ending child marriage.
